subject: Tiered routing design sprint — kickoff availability + prework
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@orbitai.com>, Patricia Gomez <pgomez@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Tiered routing design sprint — kickoff availability + prework

Hi Alex / Patricia,

Thanks again for agreeing to run the hands-on routing policy design sprint with us. We want to use the kickoff to align on model choices, tiering, and fallback rules so the later lab slot can focus on prompt pass-throughs and the load test run.

Can you share 60–90 minutes when your infra and product folks can join next week? Our suggested windows (PST):
- Tues 11/24: 10:00–11:30 or 14:00–15:30
- Wed 11/25: 09:00–10:30 or 15:00–16:30

Prework we’ll do on our side: a short draft routing playbook (attached) and a loadtest plan. Please review the routing-playbook-v1.pdf and add any model constraints you need (e.g., on-prem model only, quantization preferences).

Proposed agenda (draft):
1) Goals & success criteria (10m)
2) Model selection & tier mapping (20m)
3) Fallback rules & regional routing (20m)
4) Load test window & runbook (15m)
5) Actions & next steps (15m)

If you prefer we can split into a short alignment + follow-up working session. Let me know what works.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: routing-playbook-v1.pdf, loadtest-plan.xlsx
From: Patricia Gomez <pgomez@acme-corp.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Alex Nguyen <alex@orbitai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tiered routing design sprint — kickoff availability + prework

Hi Sean,

Thanks — the agenda looks good. We can do Wed 11/25 at 15:00 PST but our infra lead will only be available for the first 60 minutes. Can we prioritize model selection and fallback rules in the first hour?

A few quick calls-outs for prework:
- We run a mix of hosted and on-prem models. On-prem models must remain in-region (eu-west) for PHI workloads.
- Can you confirm whether prefix caching will be enabled during the load tests?

If you need internal contacts, loop in our platform lead (I’ll add them if required).

—Patricia
Patricia Gomez
Head of Product Ops | Acme Corp
pgomez@acme-corp.com | +1 (212) 555-3344
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tiered routing design sprint — kickoff availability + prework

Patricia — thanks, that works.

We’ll prioritize model selection and fallback rules in the first 60 minutes and keep the loadtest/runbook discussion to the last 30 (or separate follow-up if the infra lead needs to hop off). To answer your question: prefix/KV caching will be off for the first exploratory passes but we’ll run a second pass with caching enabled to measure SLO impact — we’ll note that in the loadtest-plan.xlsx.

I’ve attached a short meeting-agenda.md and the routing-playbook-v1.pdf for in-thread comments. Please add any region-specific constraints (e.g., eu-west-only models) directly in the doc or reply here.

Draft invite: Wed 11/25, 15:00–16:30 PST — Zoom link + calendar invite to follow once we confirm.

Sean

Quick operational note:

If we lock Wed 11/25 15:00 PST, our recommended loadwindow for the follow-on run is Thu 11/26 02:00–04:00 UTC (low external traffic, gives us time to collect traces). For the actual load run we’ll need:
- a stable seed prompt set (~250 prompts)
- target concurrency and token ceiling per model (put into loadtest-plan.xlsx)
- confirmation of which model variants are acceptable fallbacks (e.g., llama-2-13b-8bit as a fallback for larger 70B variants)

Patricia — if you can paste the list of in-scope models (or share a short doc link) we’ll fill the tier mapping and include quantization recommendations.

—Karthik
